subject: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <storres@edge-sys.com>, security@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments

Folks —

Following the kickoff with Acme this morning, we need to align on a recommended, supportable pattern for sending logs + traces from Redwood Private stacks in customer VPCs / on‑prem. Acme's security team is explicit: no egress to public endpoints except TLS to their vetted SIEM collector. They also want low-risk rollout steps so ops can validate.

High-level ask: produce a concise runbook that covers three deployment options, network requirements, and tracing header propagation. Draft proposal attached (redwood-log-export-profiles-v1.xlsx). Please review these three patterns and call out residual risks:

- Agent-in-VPC (OpenTelemetry collector sidecar/daemonset) forwarding to customer SIEM endpoint (mTLS)
- Connector-proxy (Redwood-managed collector in dedicated subnet peered to customer VPC) with explicit firewall rules
- Syslog/Trap push via customer SIEM gateway (hosted appliances) for legacy partners

Questions for the thread:
1) Which pattern should be prescriptive for new customers?
2) Minimum port/IP rules we must recommend for security teams (CIDR, TLS, SNI expectations)
3) Tracing: how do we guarantee trace ids survive model routing (multi-model fanout)?

Assigning: Marcus, draft the network requirements; Vivek, enumerate support matrix (who owns endpoints / fallback). Monica, coordinate validation steps with Acme security.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <storres@edge-sys.com>, security@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments

Irene —

Quick update after a technical review: attached is a network sketch (otlp-collector-network-diff.png) and the baseline port table in the spreadsheet. Summary of my recommendations:

1) Default pattern: Agent (OpenTelemetry collector) inside customer VPC as a daemonset/sidecar. Reasons: minimal cross‑account networking, trace/span enrichment close to host, easier to meet egress restrictions.

2) Connector (proxy) pattern for customers who want Redwood to manage collector lifecycle. This requires:
   - Dedicated peered subnet or PrivateLink equivalent.
   - Static egress IPs from our connector pool (we must publish IPs to customer).
   - mTLS terminator in customer SIEM (cert exchange + short rotation window).

3) Syslog push for legacy SIEMs: supported but will lose structured trace/attribute fidelity. Recommend only for logs; traces should not be sent via syslog.

Network defaults (for documentation):
- TLS (443) with SNI matching the collector host (collector.acme.example or our connector endpoint)
- OTLP/gRPC fallback port 4317 only when both sides agree in the M&A
- Collector health: allow inbound from customer ops IP range for debugging (SSH/HTTPS to management plane)

Risks:
- Agent pattern increases customer-side operational burden (upgrades, resource usage).
- Connector pattern requires strict IP publishing and capacity planning to avoid SNAT/port exhaustion.

I'll put these into a one‑page network checklist. Marcus
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <storres@edge-sys.com>, security@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments

Thanks Marcus — a few practical notes from support and SRE ops:

- Tracing: ensure we always propagate our internal traceparent and baggage fields across the model routing layer. Action: implement an OTLP header passthrough at the model router and include a small reconciliation service that rehydrates spans dropped by third-party inference frontends.

- Sampling: default to 1% for customer-managed collectors; provide a whitelist for high-value flows (interactive sessions) where we sample at 10%. Document how to change this via the customer config in the private control plane.

- Retries: otlp/gRPC retries must be bounded; when the collector is unreachable, buffer to disk but cap at X GB per node and expose an operator metric (telemetry.buffer_drops).

- Redaction: PII redaction at source is customer responsibility, but include an operator hook in our collector config to apply basic JSON key scrubbing (config flag).

- Rollout plan: Canary with one customer VPC subnet, synthetic trace generation to exercise fanout, confirm trace ids intact end-to-end.

I'll draft the support matrix and tie it to our SLAs. Vivek
From: Sam Torres <storres@edge-sys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments

Appreciate the clarity. A couple notes from Edge Sys (we build lightweight OTEL collectors that Acme uses):

- mTLS handshake: prefer cert pinning rather than client CN checks; we'll exchange fingerprints with Acme.
- Heartbeat: we'd like an occasional short (1KB) heartbeat to the connector so we can quickly identify SNAT or route issues; 5m cadence suggested.
- Span fidelity: if you route through a connector that alters timing, please add a stamped wall_time field so we can rebase in the SIEM.

We'll test the OTLP/gRPC + TLS handshake against the otlp collector image you shared. Sam
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <storres@edge-sys.com>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 17:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design: Tracing + Log Export Patterns for Private VPC / On‑Prem Deployments

Looping back with the validation checklist we ran with Acme security this morning — they validated the agent-in-VPC approach as preferred, provided we meet three guardrails:

1) Published minimal egress policy (CIDR + ports) for their auditors — we used Marcus's table and tightened the allowed IPs to a /28 for the connector pool where used.
2) mTLS with cert rotation cadence <= 90 days and cert pinning support.
3) Evidence of trace continuity during model fanout: we ran synthetic traffic and validated span ids in their SIEM for 10k requests—no breaks observed when otlp collector was local.

Next steps (short):
- Finalize the one‑page network checklist and include exact iptables/sg rules snippets (Marcus)
- Create a small test harness that injects traces at the routing layer (Vivek) and capture the proof artifacts we send to Acme security
- Update the customer runbook and the Private Control Plane config UI to expose sampling + scrubbing toggles (Irene/Monica)

Attaching the acceptance notes and the test artefact links to the Drive doc. I'll coordinate a short runbook handoff meeting with Acme ops on Thursday.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
